The sync is scheduled hourly without `withoutOverlapping()`. Laravel starts each hourly invocation independently, so a peak run lasting up to 45 minutes can overlap with the next scheduled execution, causing duplicate API calls and webhook notifications.
Fix the schedule by adding a cache-backed overlap lock with an expiry that covers the documented runtime while preserving the hourly cadence, for example:
```php
Schedule::command('app:sync-marketplace')
    ->hourly()
    ->withoutOverlapping(60);
```
`onOneServer()` may also be appropriate if multiple scheduler servers run, but it does not replace `withoutOverlapping()` for this issue.
<diagnosis>
Root cause: the hourly marketplace sync has no overlap prevention. Mechanism: Laravel launches the next hourly command even when the previous peak-window execution is still running, producing duplicate imports, API load, and webhook notifications. Fix: add `withoutOverlapping()` using a cache-backed lock, with an expiry of at least the documented 45-minute runtime—60 minutes is suitable—while retaining the hourly schedule; add `onOneServer()` as well if the scheduler runs on multiple servers.
</diagnosis>

## Context
TradeLoop pulls orders from its marketplace into the local store through the app:sync-marketplace command, scheduled hourly. Ops has documented that the sync legitimately runs up to 45 minutes during peak windows (the constant on the command is the contract). A duplicate import is not fatal for data (upserts) but it doubles the API load and triggers double webhook notifications to merchants — merchants have complained about receiving every notification twice.
## Reported problem
Merchants report that during peak windows every order notification arrives twice, exactly one hour apart, and our API dashboards show the sync running in two overlapping executions. Ops confirmed the sync can legitimately take 45 minutes during peaks — that is part of the command's contract. Review the scheduling of the sync and make overlapping executions impossible without breaking the hourly cadence or the documented runtime expectations.
